title: Measuring the Solar System
objective: After this level you can explain the astronomical unit and how astronomers measured the size of the solar system.
summary: Kepler gave the solar system’s shape; transits of Venus and later radar gave its size: 1 AU ≈ 150 million km.

cards.headline: Knowing the shape of the solar system isn’t the same as knowing its size.
A map without a scale
cards.body: Kepler’s laws told astronomers the relative distances of the planets: Mars is about 1.5 times farther from the Sun than Earth, for example. But without one real distance in kilometers, the map had no scale. Every distance in the solar system depended on that one missing number.

cards.headline: Chasing Venus
cards.body: In 1761 and 1769, astronomers spread around the world to time Venus crossing the face of the Sun. Comparing their views let them work out the Earth–Sun distance. Today radar and spacecraft pin it down very precisely.

cards.fact: 1 astronomical unit (AU) is about 150 million km.
cards.context: It’s the average Earth–Sun distance, and the solar system’s standard yardstick.

cards.headline: Solar system: measured
learned: Kepler gave relative distances, not a scale
Transits of Venus (1761, 1769) set the scale
Radar and spacecraft now measure it precisely

questions.explanation: One astronomical unit is the average Earth–Sun distance, about 150 million km.

questions.prompt: Why did astronomers still need to measure one real distance after Kepler?

options.label: Kepler’s laws gave proportions but no kilometers
Kepler’s laws had turned out to be wrong
options.rationale: His laws were right; they lacked a scale.

options.label: To search for new planets beyond Saturn
options.rationale: The goal was the size of the known system.

options.label: To measure the exact speed of light
options.rationale: The goal was the Earth–Sun distance.

questions.explanation: Kepler’s laws fixed the proportions of the solar system. One measured distance, like the Earth–Sun distance, set the scale for all of it.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. What distance does that light cover?

options.label: About 1 light-year
options.rationale: Light takes a full year for that.

questions.explanation: Sunlight crosses the Earth–Sun distance, 1 AU or about 150 million km, in about 8 minutes.
